actions.title: REDACTED: a HIGH severity finding in the security lens is withheld from the public copy. See this project's own bar-raise report for detail.

Point the queue lock at the literal shared lock path rather than deriving it by appending to the data filename; the server locks .work-queue.json.lock while both sanctioned writers lock .work-queue.lock, so console queue writes are not serialised against them and the test mirrors the same wrong derivation.

Write a status sync step for this project, or fold the pointer refresh into write-dashboard-status.ps1; the audit block names a 2026-08-07 report that no longer exists and its finding counts match no report on disk, across at least four audit cycles.

Replace the in-daily-use claim in README.md and DESIGN.md with the measured cadence; the run archive holds 15 receipts across 5 distinct dates in 66 days with a 21-day dry spell, and that claim is what justifies treating the milestone as shipped.

Rule keep or kill on the hourly drain and correct the queue item that closed itself by asserting a retirement that never happened; the drain has been silent 20 days and the health watcher still lists the decision as open. [CHRONIC]

Replace the synchronous lock backoff with an async retry; it can stall the single-threaded event loop for up to 8 seconds, exceeding the watchdog health timeout and killing live run streams. [CHRONIC]

Scope the nightly retention step to the report types each routine generates and give bar-raise reports their own pass; the queue item asking for this has been blocked-on-user with zero attempts since 2026-08-13. [CHRONIC]
Protect docs/drift-fixes-2026-08-01.md; it is the sole gitignored copy of its report type, exactly the shape the nightly retention step destroyed three nights running in three other projects.

Extract one shared output-pump helper so the script route gets the same partial-line buffering the run and new-project routes already have; this is the path that gives release and push confirmations from the phone. [CHRONIC]
Narrow the canonical-audit trigger description so a bare audit-a-project phrase stops mapping ambiguously to three skills; verified unfixed at source, not just in a snapshot. [CHRONIC]
Add hard-rule assertions to check-readiness.ps1 and call it as a gate in release.ps1; the new test suite covers helper functions, not one of the four hard rules. [CHRONIC]
Add this project to the git recovery skill repo map; the branch-reference lock half landed on 2026-08-14 but the recovery runbook still cannot recognise this repo by name. [CHRONIC]
Add this project to the decision-promoter routing table and the code-audit supported list, plus a per-project hazard file; both still fall through to the unhandled path. [CHRONIC]

Move terminal queue items to the archive from a routine that actually runs; completed rows grew from 53 to 230 because the only routine that ever pruned them is the disabled drain. Promptless half verified fixed at zero. [CHRONIC]
Add a priority picker beside the queue button; every queued item silently defaults to the middle priority regardless of urgency. [CHRONIC]
Add a queue panel and a read endpoint; after queuing, the console shows one toast and then offers no way to see, reprioritise or cancel what is pending.
Split or relabel the runs-archived metric; it reads 15 while the usage ledger bills 171 sessions, because the hourly credential probe writes no receipt. [CHRONIC]
Update the README cost model to the corrected wording; the design doc and handler both flagged the monthly-credit description as wrong on 2026-08-19 and the fix never reached the public-facing file.
Widen the run-receipt secret scrub; the archive already contains a real password-recovery session that reads clean only because someone redacted it by hand later, not because the scrub matched it.

Rule on which projection tier this project belongs to; its public status file still ships full finding text naming live security gaps, the exposure class that moved two other projects to a restricted tier on 2026-08-19.

Delete or resync the older skills snapshot; it holds a handler-audit definition claiming a four-handler scope that omits this project entirely, and if that copy resolves the handler sweep silently skips this repo.

Teach the health watcher that a task-running result code is the correct steady state for a permanent watchdog loop, and cross-check the live heartbeat before flagging red; the current rule produces a standing false alarm on a server that is verifiably up.
